- document attachment handling and add runtime/workflow coverage

- `git diff --check`

Closes #426

## AI Review Synthesis

<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis -->
<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis-head: 487b2b404cbb9c881252ec7f3155b91d6bba4a88 -->

> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue
PR #428 implements issue #426 by downloading GitHub `user-attachments` before the agent runs, using the resolved GitHub token, and passing a local manifest into the prompt. The goal is to make private-repo attachments readable without exposing tokens to the model or relying on unauthenticated fetches. The implementation adds a shared scanner/downloader, wires it into `run-agent-task`, updates the base prompt, and adds focused docs/tests. The current design is well placed on the shared runtime path, but the current diff still has one correctness gap for resumed sessions and two robustness issues on the shared pre-agent path.

## Review
Overall, the PR is directionally solid and matches the linked issue plan, but it should not ship until resumed runs receive the attachment manifest. Reviewers disagreed on severity: the rubrics review passed with no warnings, while the code reviews identified concrete runtime issues; the resumed-session gap is supported by the current PR head.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Resumed sessions lose attachment manifests | BLOCKING | The manifest is injected only into the full/base prompt, but resumed persistent sessions use the lightweight continuation prompt, which does not include `ATTACHMENTS_MANIFEST` or local-path instructions. |
| Attachment enrichment can fail all agent runs | WARNING | The new shared attachment step lacks `continue-on-error: true`, so top-level CLI failures can stop the composite action before the agent runs. |
| Attachment downloads lack resource bounds | WARNING | The downloader buffers each response with `arrayBuffer()` and has no file-size cap, attachment-count cap, or fetch timeout for URLs collected from issue/PR/discussion text. |

## Progress
- PR already implements the shared scanner/downloader, manifest injection, prompt guidance, docs, and targeted runtime/workflow tests.
- Rubrics review reported PASS and no rubric-specific follow-up.
- Existing inline comments and review threads were empty before synthesis.
- Posted three inline comments for the concrete changed-line issues: `.agent/src/run.ts#L414`, `.github/actions/run-agent-task/action.yml#L342`, and `.agent/src/attachments.ts#L558`.

## Issue Details
<details>
<summary>Resumed sessions lose attachment manifests</summary>

**Cause:** `run.ts` reads `ATTACHMENTS_MANIFEST` into `promptVars`, then renders the full prompt, but resumed sessions can pass `buildContinuationPrompt(...)` to `runAcpx`. `buildContinuationPrompt` only includes trigger metadata, optional answer-review context, and `REQUEST_TEXT`, so follow-up `/answer` or `/fix-pr` runs can download an attachment without telling the agent the `localPath`.

**Candidate solutions:** Include the attachment manifest section in continuation prompts, or force full prompt replay when a manifest exists. Add `prompt-continuation.test.ts` coverage for an attachment-bearing resumed run.

**Comments:** This is the main reviewer disagreement: rubrics passed, but the current runtime code confirms the resumed prompt path drops the new manifest context.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Attachment enrichment can fail all agent runs</summary>

**Cause:** The `Download GitHub attachments` step is on the shared `run-agent-task` path and lacks `continue-on-error: true`. Per-file download errors are captured in the manifest, but top-level failures such as output directory creation, manifest writing, or `setOutput` can still reject and fail the action.

**Candidate solutions:** Make the step non-fatal with `continue-on-error: true`, matching nearby best-effort enrichment steps, and rely on the existing `run.ts` missing-manifest fallback.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Attachment downloads lack resource bounds</summary>

**Cause:** `downloadGitHubAttachments` fetches every collected URL sequentially and buffers the full body with `await response.arrayBuffer()` before writing to disk. There is no cap on response size, number of references, or request duration.

**Candidate solutions:** Add a maximum attachment count, a per-file size cap using `Content-Length` plus a guarded read, and a fetch timeout such as `AbortSignal.timeout(...)`. Record over-limit and timeout failures as manifest errors instead of failing the run.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
FIX_PR: The unresolved issues are concrete branch changes suitable for an automated fix-pr pass.

## Final Verdict
NEEDS_REWORK

## Action Items
- [ ] Ensure resumed-session continuation prompts include the attachment manifest/local-path guidance, or replay the full prompt when a manifest exists, with regression coverage.
- [ ] Make the shared attachment download step non-fatal so best-effort enrichment cannot block every agent run.
- [ ] Add attachment download size, count, and timeout bounds while preserving manifest-level error reporting.

---

Ok the first q that i want to ask is, does it only download the file in the latest comment or all past comments? 

I think this causes a broader issue: what if agents keep searching for all issues for files? We cannot exhaust everything right? 

But the way seems to provide the environment key to download the file? Or? We are a customized and protected file download command? What to do?

It currently scans **all past comments on the current target**, not only the latest comment.

For PR #428 specifically, `collectAttachmentTextSources` scans:

- forwarded `REQUEST_TEXT`
- issue body + issue comments
- PR body + issue comments + PR reviews + PR review comments
- discussion body + discussion comments/replies

See the current PR code around [`attachments.ts#L317-L395`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/487b2b404cbb9c881252ec7f3155b91d6bba4a88/.agent/src/attachments.ts#L317-L395). It dedupes attachment URLs by exact URL before downloading: [`attachments.ts#L161-L188`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/487b2b404cbb9c881252ec7f3155b91d6bba4a88/.agent/src/attachments.ts#L161-L188).

It **does not search all issues in the repo**. It only queries the current issue/PR/discussion target number passed into `run-agent-task`. So the broader “agents searching every issue for files” concern is real in principle, but this PR does not implement that behavior.

On auth: yes, this is meant to be a customized protected pre-agent download path. The action passes the resolved GitHub token only to the downloader step: [`run-agent-task/action.yml#L342-L354`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/487b2b404cbb9c881252ec7f3155b91d6bba4a88/.github/actions/run-agent-task/action.yml#L342-L354). The downloader uses it as an `Authorization: Bearer ...` header: [`attachments.ts#L529-L536`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/487b2b404cbb9c881252ec7f3155b91d6bba4a88/.agent/src/attachments.ts#L529-L536). The prompt only receives the manifest/local paths, not the token: [`_base.md#L12-L19`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/487b2b404cbb9c881252ec7f3155b91d6bba4a88/.github/prompts/_base.md#L12-L19).

What I’d do before merging:

1. Keep downloader scope bounded to the **current target thread only**.
2. Add hard limits: max attachment count, max bytes per file, and fetch timeout.
3. Make the downloader best-effort so failures produce manifest errors instead of blocking the whole agent run.
4. Optionally narrow policy further: for `issue_comment` triggers, download only `REQUEST_TEXT` plus target body by default, and scan older comments only if we decide that cross-comment attachments are important enough.

My recommendation: keep current-target scanning, but add the resource limits. Do **not** add repo-wide issue search for attachments.

Yes, we can go deeper, but I’d separate two meanings of “protected command”:

1. **Current PR model: protected pre-download**
   - Before the agent starts, `run-agent-task` runs a downloader with the GitHub token.
   - The agent only receives a manifest of local files.
   - This is the cleanest version because the model never needs to decide how to authenticate attachment downloads.
   - Current PR shape: [`download-attachments.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/487b2b404cbb9c881252ec7f3155b91d6bba4a88/.agent/src/cli/download-attachments.ts#L34-L77), prompt manifest injection in [`_base.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/487b2b404cbb9c881252ec7f3155b91d6bba4a88/.github/prompts/_base.md#L12-L19).

2. **Agent-callable protected download command**
   - We could expose a command in the prompt, but it should **not** be `download any URL`.
   - It should be something like:
     ```bash
     node .agent/dist/cli/attachment.js get --id attachment-003
     ```
   - The command should only download URLs already discovered from the current target thread and written into a manifest/allowlist.
   - It should reject arbitrary URLs, cross-repo URLs, excessive size, too many files, and timeouts.

The important caveat: a CLI alone is **not a hard security boundary** if the agent process also has the raw GitHub token in its environment. In the current runtime, `run-agent-task` passes GitHub auth into the agent step for normal repo operations. So a “protected command” is useful for policy, auditability, limits, and better behavior, but it does not fully prevent a sufficiently capable shell agent from using credentials elsewhere.

So my recommendation is:

- For this PR: keep the **pre-download + manifest** design.
- Make it bounded: current target only, max count, max size, timeout, best-effort failure.
- Do **not** expose a general URL downloader.
- If we later want a true protected interactive downloader, design it as a broker:
  - token is not placed in the agent environment,
  - agent can only request files by manifest ID,
  - broker enforces target/repo allowlist and limits,
  - all downloads are logged into the manifest.

So the short answer is: yes, “customized protected file download command” is a good direction, but for now I’d treat this PR’s pre-agent downloader as the safer first version. A command shared in the prompt should only operate on pre-approved manifest entries, not arbitrary attachment URLs.

`codex` | `gpt-5.5` | `high` | `Macmini-runner-3`

@sepo-agent /answer can we implement this version directly without the preloaded (we should explore this as a completely direction -- branching out from main and workin on that).

Yes, but “directly without preload” should mean **no pre-downloading file bytes**, not “no pre-run setup at all”.

We still need a pre-agent **index/allowlist** step, because the protected command needs to know which attachment IDs are allowed. The better branch direction from `main` would be:

1. Add an attachment indexer:
   - scans only the current target thread,
   - records discovered `github.com/user-attachments/...` URLs,
   - writes a manifest like:
     ```json
     {
       "attachments": [
         {
           "id": "attachment-001",
           "url": "...",
           "sources": [...],
           "status": "available"
         }
       ]
     }
     ```
   - does **not** download file contents yet.

2. Add an agent-callable command:
   ```bash
   node .agent/dist/cli/attachment.js get --id attachment-001
   ```
   This command should:
   - accept only manifest IDs, not raw URLs,
   - reject IDs not in the current-run manifest,
   - enforce max count, max size, timeout, and current repo/target constraints,
   - download to `$RUNNER_TEMP/agent-attachments/`,
   - update the manifest with `localPath`, size, content type, and errors.

3. Update the prompt to say:
   - use `attachment.js list` to inspect available attachments,
   - use `attachment.js get --id ...` to fetch one,
   - do not fetch original `github.com/user-attachments` URLs directly.

The hard part: today `run-agent-task` passes `INPUT_GITHUB_TOKEN` into the agent step, and `buildSharedEnv()` mirrors it to `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN`: [`runtime-env.ts#L29-L35`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/runtime-env.ts#L29-L35). So a CLI wrapper is not a true security boundary while the agent also has raw GitHub auth. It is still useful for policy and auditability, but not fully “protected”.

So I’d split implementation into two phases:

- **Phase 1:** implement on-demand download by manifest ID, with limits and logging. This replaces preloaded file bytes.
- **Phase 2:** make it truly protected by changing the auth boundary: do not pass raw GitHub token into the agent, or introduce a local broker process that holds the token and only serves allowlisted attachment IDs.

My recommendation: create a new branch from `main` for this direction, not continue PR #428 as-is. PR #428 is the “pre-download manifest” design; this would be a cleaner alternate design: **pre-index only, download on demand by allowlisted ID**.

@sepo-agent /answer

Yes, we can implement this as a new direction from `main`: **no preloaded files, no indexer, just an agent-callable download command**.

I would still narrow “any given GitHub URL” to **any GitHub user-attachment URL**:

```bash
node .agent/dist/cli/download-github-attachment.js \
  --url "https://github.com/user-attachments/files/..."
```

The command should:

- accept a raw URL from the agent,
- validate `https://github.com/user-attachments/(files|assets)/...`,
- reject non-GitHub and non-attachment URLs,
- download using `INPUT_GITHUB_TOKEN` / `GH_TOKEN`,
- enforce max file size, timeout, and safe filename handling,
- write to `$RUNNER_TEMP/agent-attachments/`,
- print the local path and metadata.

I would **not** make it a general authenticated `github.com` downloader. That becomes too close to “authenticated curl for anything GitHub can access.” Attachment URLs are the real problem, so the command should be attachment-specific.

Current architecture fit:

- `run-agent-task` already passes `INPUT_GITHUB_TOKEN` into the agent step: [`run-agent-task/action.yml#L342-L351`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/actions/run-agent-task/action.yml#L342-L351)
- `buildSharedEnv()` mirrors that into `GH_TOKEN` / `GITHUB_TOKEN`: [`runtime-env.ts#L29-L35`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/runtime-env.ts#L29-L35)
- the base prompt already documents token handling boundaries: [`_base.md#L28-L31`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/prompts/_base.md#L28-L31)

So this version is simpler than PR #428:

1. Add `.agent/src/cli/download-github-attachment.ts`.
2. Add a small shared helper for URL validation, filename sanitization, fetch timeout, and size cap.
3. Update `_base.md` to tell agents: use this command for `github.com/user-attachments` links; do not use raw `curl`/browser fetches for private attachments.
4. Add tests for valid attachment URLs, rejected URLs, missing token, timeout, oversized response, filename handling, and successful download.
5. Update docs for the command.

I’d close or supersede PR #428 and branch from `main` for this alternate design. It gives us the behavior you want without scanning all past comments and without pre-downloading anything.
